$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.

plan.intent: Fix guard-builder-scope.py misresolving MSYS/Cygwin paths. ONE helper (e.g. _from_msys) called as the first step INSIDE norm(), active only when os.name == 'nt': a string matching ^/([A-Za-z])(/|$) or ^/cygdrive/([A-Za-z])(/|$) becomes '<X>:/' + rest; anything else is returned unchanged. Yes to /cygdrive/c (same regex, zero cost); NO to /mnt/c (WSL). norm() is already the single normaliser for the Write branch, the Bash branch, approved_paths and transient_roots, so the branches cannot drift. In bash_targets normalise the base BEFORE the join: base = norm(cwd) if cwd is a non-empty str else UMBRELLA; then norm(target if isabs else join(base, target)). This also fixes absolute MSYS targets (/c/Users/...), which isabs() accepts as rooted and realpath maps to C:/c/Users/... today. Fail-closed invariants, each pinned by a test: an unrecognised cwd (/zz/x, relative/dir, //c/x) passes through unchanged and is judged exactly as before; realpath still runs after the join so '..' is resolved before matching and traversal out of the approved set is denied; no new early-return/allow branch; main() exception handler still denies. Regression tests in the existing test_guard_builder_scope.py, run when os.name == 'nt', MSYS spelling derived from UMBRELLA (never hard-coded): (1) relative approved target, MSYS cwd of huntstack/apps/mobile + 'echo x > App.tsx' -> allow; (2) same with /cygdrive/c cwd -> allow; (3) relative unapproved target with MSYS cwd of huntstack/apps/web -> deny; (4) '..' traversal from an MSYS cwd inside the approved dir to an unapproved sibling -> deny; (5) absolute MSYS-spelled target: approved -> allow, unapproved -> deny; (6) Write payload with MSYS-spelled file_path: approved -> allow, unapproved -> deny; (7) unrecognised cwd /zz/nope with an unapproved relative target -> deny; (8) /cc/x is not treated as a drive. Update the norm() docstring and the comment above base =.

findings.issue: FAIL-OPEN. base = norm(cwd) strips the root separator: norm rstrips '/', so a drive-root cwd ('/c/', '/c', '/cygdrive/c/', and plain Windows 'C:\' or 'C:/') becomes 'c:'. os.path.join('c:', rel) is DRIVE-RELATIVE ('c:huntstack/...'), so realpath resolves it against the HOOK PROCESS cwd, not the shell's. Concrete: approved huntstack/apps/mobile/**, Bash payload cwd='/c/' (or 'C:\'), command 'echo x > huntstack/apps/mobile/App.tsx' -> the shell writes C:\huntstack\apps\mobile\App.tsx (outside the set); the guard resolves it to repos/huntstack/apps/mobile/app.tsx and ALLOWS. End to end via the suite's own hook_decision: all 5 root spellings x 2 hook cwds -> allow on fu-s2, deny on master. A plain Windows root cwd is a regression independent of MSYS. Also mis-resolves the other way: cwd '/c/' + '../../Windows/x' -> c:/users/natha/windows/x. The Bash tool's cwd persists between calls, so 'cd /c/' in one call then a relative write in the next reaches this. Fix: do not pre-norm the base -- join(_from_msys(cwd), target) and norm once after, or keep a trailing separator on a root base. Add a drive-root-cwd deny check.

Item 4 (non-Windows unchanged) does not hold for the same reason: on POSIX norm('/') -> '' and join('', rel) -> rel, resolved against the hook process cwd. A cwd of '/' with 'echo x > huntstack/apps/mobile/App.tsx' allows when the hook runs in repos/. Derived with posixpath, not run on a POSIX host. Same fix closes it.

Builder deviation (_from_msys(target) before isabs) is sound: on 3.13 Windows isabs('/c/x') is False, so without it an absolute MSYS target would be joined onto the base. _from_msys is a no-op on its own output, Write and Bash reach the same norm() result for the same spelling, no new return/allow path, inside the approved file set.

findings.detail: Attempt-1 blocker closed. I tested approved huntstack/apps/mobile/** with 'echo x > huntstack/apps/mobile/App.tsx' and cwd in {/c/, /c, /cygdrive/c/, /cygdrive/c, C:\, C:/, C:, c:, c:foo, C:huntstack, /}, with the hook process cwd at repos, Temp and C:\Windows. All 33 cases DENY through the real hook. The base is no longer norm()'d, so a root cwd keeps its separator (c:/ + rel is absolute).

The unmatchable marker is sound. It is a raw string beginning with '<', and it is never passed through norm(). _match needs equality or a prefix of a norm()'d approved path (which starts with a drive letter), or an fnmatch pattern that also starts with the umbrella or an absolute drive path. worktree_context(marker) can never see the target under root+'/'. Probes with crafted cwds all deny: one embeds the marker text, one is 'c:<lowercased approved path>', one is c:'<approved path>. Absolute targets under a drive-relative cwd are still judged normally: an approved one allows, an unapproved one denies.

Tightenings, which are intended. (a) A bare 'C:' cwd plus a relative approved name was ALLOWED on master. Master also allowed c:foo and C:huntstack when the hook ran in Temp, because Windows resolves them against the inherited per-drive cwd. All of these now DENY. (b) A relative or rooted-no-drive target under a drive-relative cwd (e.g. cwd 'c:' with '> /tmp/x') is now denied rather than skipped as a temp sink, because the marker is appended before the transient check. The harness never sends a drive-relative cwd, so this is acceptable.

'Joined raw as master does' holds literally. For a cwd that does not match the MSYS regex, _from_msys returns it unchanged. posixpath.splitdrive is always '', so on POSIX base == cwd exactly as on master and the '/' cwd is the same as master (it is a fix relative to 4bf34db, not a tightening relative to master). Pre-existing and unchanged on both master and fu-s2: a relative cwd ('huntstack', 'relative/dir') resolves against the hook process cwd. The harness sends absolute cwds, so this is not a blocker for this slice.
